title: The Case System — Third Look (مَمْنُوع مِنَ الصَّرْف)

steps.title: The last irregular layer — and its own exception
body: Diptotes (مَمْنُوع مِنَ الصَّرْف) are a closed set of noun shapes — certain broken-plural patterns like مَفَاعِل and أَفْعِلَاء, and every proper name of a person — that never take tanwīn.
When INDEFINITE, a diptote takes ḍamma for رَفْع and fatḥa for both نَصْب and جَرّ — so its جَرّ form looks exactly like its نَصْب form, and neither has the tanwīn a regular noun would have.

But that irregularity has its own exception: the moment a diptote becomes DEFINITE — by الـ, or by being the second term of an إِضَافَة whose own definiteness carries through — it declines completely regularly again, kasra included. هَذَا بَيْتُ أَصْدِقَاءَ (indefinite, fatḥa) vs. هَذَا بَيْتُ الْأَصْدِقَاءِ (definite, kasra) is the same noun, the same جَرّ role, two different markers.

steps.title: The exception to the exception
steps.arabicPrompt: هَذَا بَيْتُ أَصْدِقَاءَ  /  هَذَا بَيْتُ الْأَصْدِقَاءِ
steps.prompt: Both أَصْدِقَاءَ and الْأَصْدِقَاءِ are جَرّ here. Which pair of markers is correct?

options.label: Both take fatḥa — diptotes never take kasra
Both take kasra — الـ has no effect on diptotes

steps.explanation: A diptote only shows its irregular fatḥa-for-جَرّ marker when INDEFINITE. Add الـ — or make it the second term of an إِضَافَة whose own definiteness carries through, as it does here — and it takes the regular kasra like any other noun.

steps.title: The full case system, on nouns
steps.message: Regular nouns, the five nouns, the sound plurals, and now diptotes — every noun-marking pattern in الإِعْرَاب. Case marking on the verb itself (رفع/نصب/جزم of the present tense) is a separate system, still ahead.
